text: Target Architecture v7 keeps the 92-table reading of version 6 slide 11 exactly as written and states, on the new data slide, that the Ownership Map v1 carries 93 rows (87 business tables and 6 platform library tables); the 93-row count is the target for the build.
why: R-PREC puts the Architecture v5 catalogue above the story masters, the Ownership Map assigns one owner to every table and the physical schema work builds from the Map, while the next version may not change a number of the source slide it keeps.
read: A reader sees both counts and the reason: 92 is the monolith count kept unchanged, 93 is the target (87 plus the 6 library tables created in every schema).
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 12 (kept unchanged) and slide 28 (Data: one ACE database, 19 schemas, no data lake)
impact: The dictionary object count and the physical schema file differ by the 6 library tables until the data architect confirms the target count.

text: The settings of the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 (partitions, replication factor, retention, key, schema subject, ACLs) are carried as the placeholder of Template and Rules R9 in the deck and are not invented.
why: Architecture v5 gives the full Kafka settings for the 19 service topics and none for the shared topic, and an invented setting would be cited by the event documents and by every service story that publishes a decision record.
read: A build team knows the topic name, the producer (all 19 services), the consumer (rwb-decision) and the five-minute completeness target; the topic settings stay open until the Kafka platform team confirms them.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 26 (Kafka: one topic per service, outbox and inbox)
impact: The shared topic cannot be created with a policy until the settings are confirmed; the producer and consumer contracts are unaffected.

text: gateway-bff and the partner gateway are platform edge components outside the 19 services: they have no schema, no topic and no task queue of their own, the edge epic RWB-PLT-EDGE delivers them, and the deck states that no owner code is given for them.
why: Architecture v5 counts the edge outside the 19 services and gives it no code in the service catalogue or in the Ownership Map Services sheet, and inventing a code would create a twentieth service that no source supports.
read: The edge is described by its contracts (browser entry, one hop, 2 s timeout, FAPI 2.0 for partners) and its owner is recorded as open; the edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON carries the build.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 27 (The edge: gateway-bff and the partner gateway)
impact: No story can declare a schema or a queue for the edge until its owner is named; the edge contracts themselves are unaffected.

text: Where version 6 slide 15 and the Architecture v5 wave map disagree, the Ownership Map wave governs: P8, S2, S5 and S8 are wave 2, S1, S3, S4 and S6 are wave 3, S7 and S9 are wave 4, and version 6 slide 15 keeps the features each epic adds.
why: R-PREC puts the Architecture v5 catalogue and narrative above the story masters, and the wave fixes the service epic, the contract group and the diagram band of every story.
read: The wave bands of the deck and the story plan agree with the Ownership Map; slide 15 of version 6 is read as a feature map and not as a wave map.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 29 (Delivery: waves 0 to 4, and what is still open)
impact: If the epic of first use is the wave, eight services move one wave earlier and the Day-1 allocation of wave 2 and 3 changes with them.

text: The deck states that the environment plan of version 6 slide 14 is unchanged and that the slots and quotas needed for about 38 deployments per environment are not specified in any source; the value is carried as a gap and not as a number.
why: Version 6 counts slots for one service per environment and Architecture v5 makes 19 services with an api and a worker deployment each, so the old slot count cannot be restated as the target count without inventing one.
read: The four environments, their data class and their release trigger stay as written; the slot count for the target stays open and is raised before wave 0.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 29 (Delivery: waves 0 to 4, and what is still open); version 6 slide 15 kept unchanged
impact: Wave 0 cannot be declared ready until the slots for 38 deployments exist in DEV and SIT.

text: The number of repositories is left open: the deck keeps the version 6 constraint 'one service, one repository, one front end' as the source states it and records the repository model of the target as a gap, with the service template and repositories epic RWB-PLT-TPL as the place it is settled.
why: One repository per service and one repository with 19 modules both fit Architecture v5 slide 33 ('one Helm chart and one pipeline template') and no source chooses between them.
read: The pipeline gates, the code owners and the boundary test continue to be described per service; a reader knows the repository model is not yet fixed.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 29 (Delivery: waves 0 to 4, and what is still open); version 6 slides 3, 4 and 6 kept unchanged
impact: The pipeline and code-owner stories of wave 0 cannot be written until the model is chosen.

text: The Temporal cluster, the persistence database, the namespace rwb-recovery and the workflow kit are owned by the Platform team through the epic RWB-PLT-WF (platform) and RWB-PLT-LIB (kit), and the deck names those epics because no Ownership Map code exists for them.
why: Architecture v5 slides 23, 24 and 39 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 12 all name 'platform team' as the owner and the Ownership Map has no row for the cluster, the namespace or the kit.
read: The five Temporal layers have a named owner per layer: the Platform team for L1 to L3 and each service team for L4 and L5.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 25 (The Temporal layer: five levels, the bottom four reusable)
impact: The platform stories for the cluster and the kit have no owner code in the story plan until the epic is confirmed.

text: Target Architecture v7 is issued in Draft: no approval is recorded for this version.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment, no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing approval as an assumption.
read: The deck is complete and may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run; the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the document.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 2 (Read me, version 7 and the change log)
impact: A document that stories cite for the target architecture carries Draft status until the approval is recorded.

text: The eighteen slides of version 6 are kept unchanged in Target Architecture v7 and the realignment is carried in eleven new slides (20 to 29) after them, with a read-me slide at position 2 carrying the header, the change log and the status.
why: The work package keeps every section, ID, number and date of the source and changes only what the realignment needs, so the superseded statements stay readable next to the target that replaces them.
read: A reader sees the version 6 architecture as it was approved and then the ten changes with their ADRs; no slide of the source is lost and no number of the source is rewritten.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7, slides 2 to 19 (kept, renumbered footers) and slides 20 to 29 (new)
impact: The deck carries two readings of the same subject (for example the modular monolith on slide 7 and the 19 services on slides 21 to 23); the read-me slide states which one is the target.

text: Every release date in the deck is unchanged and marked tentative, and each service takes the release of the epic of its wave because no source gives a per-service release date.
why: Rules R1 U7 and R8.4 fix the dates as tentative and unchanged and rule 10 forbids raising a date as a gap; the per-service dates are not stated anywhere in the sources.
read: Nothing is lost. A reader sees each wave with the release of its epic, marked tentative, and no date is presented as committed.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 29 (Delivery: waves 0 to 4, and what is still open)
impact: The delivery plan has no per-service date and cannot promise one until the release plan is approved.

text: Every owner in the deck is the code taken from the Microservice Ownership Map v1 (Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs) and _work/msr/plan/ownership.json, and a Map ruling governs where one exists.
why: The work package requires the Ownership Map for every owner, and the Map is the one artefact of this run that assigns an owner to each resource with its basis and ruling.
read: Each service slide states the resources its owner code holds, with the counts of the Map; the ruling rows (for example delegation_limit to P4 and case_list_row to P1) are the ones the Map records.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slides 21, 22 and 23 (the 19 services and what each owns)
impact: Where a story master named another owner, the Map wins and the difference is recorded in the ownership work of this run.

text: The new decision rows of this version are DL44 to DL49 and the new ADRs are ADR-013 to ADR-023, as allocated in _work/msr/plan/ids.json; the deck cites them and does not write their full text.
why: Rules R8.4 fixes the ADR and Decision Log additions and the ids file allocates them after the highest used numbers (D-RCV-59, ADR-012, DL43), so no identifier is invented here.
read: A reader can follow each change in the deck to its ADR number and to the Decision Log row that records the decision.
applied_in: Target Architecture v7 slide 20 (What the realignment changes, and the ADRs that carry it) and slide 29 (new decisions DL44 to DL49)
impact: The deck depends on the ADR and Decision Log documents of this run for the full text of each decision.
